Rosa: Heads-up: sample-app CI flagged a typing error when code calls `order.status.name` — we now allow raw strings for open enums so mypy complains.
Mateo: can you paste the mypy output?
Rosa: sure:
```
src/clients/orders_client.py:88: error: Item "str" of "Union[OrderStatus, str]" has no attribute "name"  [attr-defined]
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 18 source files)
```
Anika: this is the consequence of switching to Union[Enum, str] for forward-compatibility. Two pragmatic options: add a typed accessor on the model that returns Optional[OrderStatus] (runtime still preserves raw string), or emit .pyi stubs exposing that accessor.
Mateo: I prefer a small runtime helper method `status_as_enum(self) -> Optional[OrderStatus]` that tries Enum(...) and returns None on unknown. Then user code can do `if order.status_as_enum(): ...`. Keeps runtime stable and gives clear typed path.
Jules: agreed. example patch for generator to include in models:
```
from typing import Optional, Union

class Order(BaseModel):
    status: Optional[Union[OrderStatus, str]] = None

    def status_as_enum(self) -> Optional[OrderStatus]:
        """Typed accessor: returns OrderStatus when available, otherwise None.
        Prefer this in typed code to avoid attribute errors on raw strings.
        """
        if self.status is None:
            return None
        try:
            return OrderStatus(self.status)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        except ValueError:
            return None
```
Jules: also add a tiny doc snippet in generated-file header explaining the accessor pattern and why raw strings are preserved.
Rosa: can we also add a typing test in sample-app that does `reveal_type(order.status_as_enum)` and an assertion that `order.status` can still be str at runtime? want to catch regressions.
Mateo: yes. I'll add tests: one static check (mypy reveal_type) and one runtime test simulating unknown value.

Anika: nice compromise between DX and forward compatibility. Resolving on my side. :white_check_mark:
